title: Assemble a Run That Pays One, Holds Four
scenario: It is 2:45 PM. The messy day resolves into one payment: INV-59001 to Northwind. Every value you need already lives in an artifact - the batch, the vendor master, the approval. Fill each slot by looking it up, and let the run also show the four invoices it consciously holds back.
input: Assembly rule: every slot value must come from a stored artifact. Invoice count, run total, and held count are in payment-batch.json. The pay-to name, vendor id, and bank on file are in the vendor master. The approver and approval time are in run-approval.json. The run date is day-1; funds are delivered to the Payables DL at the 3:00 PM cutoff.
instructions: Open each artifact on the shelf as you need it - do not work from memory.
Fill the header slots from the run approval (approver, time, cutoff).
Fill the batch slots from the payment batch (count, total, held).
Fill the pay-to slots from the vendor master (name, id, bank).

copilotPrompt: Assemble a payment run that pays one invoice and holds four. Look up count, total, and held from the payment batch, approver and time from the run approval, and pay-to name, vendor id, and bank from the vendor master. Do not recompute the total.
successMessage: Payment run rendered. One payment traced to artifacts, four holds shown - the run assembled by lookup alone.

sections.title: A messy day still assembles cheaply
sections.body: Even with four exceptions in play, the run is one payment. It assembles fast because the batch, vendor master, and approval already exist as trusted objects - you read them, you do not rebuild them.

sections.title: Never recompute the total
sections.body: The run total is in the payment batch. If assembly re-added invoices, the run and batch could disagree - two sources of truth. The run reads 1200 from the batch and shows the four holds it carries.

sections.title: Bank details come from the master
sections.body: The pay-to name and bank are read from the governed vendor master, never from the invoice. On a day with an unknown-vendor exception in the queue, that rule is exactly what keeps a bad payee out of the run.

takeaway.heading: Payment run assembled
points: You assembled a run that pays one invoice and shows four held, without deriving a single value.
The run is fully traceable: totals and held count to the batch, approver to the run approval, pay-to details to the vendor master.
The bank on file came from the governed master, never the invoice - the last-step fraud control.
payment-run.md is stored as a rendered document, delivered to the Payables DL at the cutoff.
The workflow can now assemble a release-ready run from upstream artifacts even when most of the day is held.
